title: Prognostic and clinicopathologic divergence in pulmonary mucinous adenocarcinoma versus nonmucinous adenocarcinoma with a mucin-laden feature.
authors: Yang F, Sun K, Li Z et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The discrepancies in clinicopathologic characteristics and prognosis between invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma (IMA) and nonmucinous lung adenocarcinoma with a mucin-laden feature (MNLA) remain unclear.
METHODS: Data were collected retospectively for 978 consecutive patients with IMA/MNLA who underwent surgical resection between October 2017 and December 2019. Survival outcomes were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and compared using the log-rank test. The adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) with 95% confidence interval (CI) of the prognosticator was calculated using a multivariable Cox proportional hazards model.
RESULTS: Pure IMA was associated with a higher prevalence of KRAS mutation (51.5%), while MNLA was associated with higher prevalences of EGFR mutation (40.4%) and EML4-ALK rearrangement (19.1%). Regarding prognosis, compared to patients with pure IMA, patients with MNLA or mixed IMA had worse disease-free survival (MNLA: aHR, 2.620, 95% CI, 1.690-4.061; mixed IMA: aHR, 3.458, 95% CI, 1.704-7.016) and overall survival (MNLA: aHR, 2.229, 95% CI, 1.185-4.193; mixed IMA: aHR, 1.723, 95% CI, 0.632-4.698). Among patients who experienced recurrence, those with pure IMA had a higher incidence of intrathoracic-only recurrence compared to those with MNLA (80.8% vs 39.6%), demonstrating that extrathoracic-only recurrence was more prevalent in MNLA (35.1% vs 7.3%). The recurrence pattern of mixed IMA was different from that of pure IMA (pure IMA vs mixed IMA: intrathoracic-only, 80.8% vs 50.0%; both intrathoracic and extrathoracic, 11.5% vs 40.0%).
CONCLUSIONS: Although MNLA, pure IMA, and mixed IMA have consistent mucin-laden features, they appear to exhibit differences in prognosis, clinicopathologic characteristics, and molecular profiles.

title: Generative design and computational characterization of pyrazoline-based EGFR kinase inhibitor candidates.
authors: Bhendarkar K, Khedekar P, Islam MA et al.
abstract: The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is an established therapeutic target in breast, colorectal, and non-small cell lung cancers, and pyrazoline-containing scaffolds have been repeatedly reported as EGFR inhibitors. This study combined generative machine learning with physics-based modelling to design and computationally characterize novel pyrazoline analogues targeting the EGFR kinase ATP-binding site. A curated set of 50 experimentally validated pyrazoline-based EGFR inhibitors, compiled from ChEMBL and the primary literature, was used to seed the Mol2Mol model in REINVENT4, generating a large library of structurally related analogues. The library was sequentially filtered according to Tanimoto similarity to the seed actives (≥0.6), predicted physicochemical, pharmacokinetic, and toxicity properties, synthetic accessibility (SA score <6), and molecular docking against the EGFR kinase domain (PDB 5U8L), using a self-docking validated protocol (redocking RMSD 1.342 Å). Five candidates, designated PyEG1-PyEG5, achieved docking scores between -9.5 and -10.6 kcal/mol, better than the redocked native ligand (-9.2 kcal/mol). All five complexes remained stable during 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations, with backbone RMSD ≤ 0.27 nm, average ligand RMSD ≤ 0.18 nm, and radii of gyration close to those of the reference complex. MM-GBSA end-point calculations yielded binding free energies of -9.9 to -37.5 kcal/mol, with PyEG5 (-37.5 ± 2.5 kcal/mol) approaching the reference ligand value (-37.6 ± 6.0 kcal/mol). Density functional theory calculations (B3LYP/6-31G(d)) indicated HOMO-LUMO gaps of 5.89-6.65 eV, with PyEG2 and PyEG5 predicted to be the most reactive and PyEG3 the most kinetically stable. Structure-activity analysis based on the predicted binding modes suggests that hinge-directed hydrogen bonding to Met793 and π-π stacking with Phe856 are the principal determinants of predicted affinity, modulated by substituent electronics and steric bulk at the R, R1, and R2 positions. These findings are entirely computational; PyEG1-PyEG5 should be considered prioritized synthetic targets, and their activity requires confirmation through biochemical kinase assays and cell-based testing.

title: Genomic characteristics and immunotherapy benefit in MSI-H/dMMR lung cancer: Insights from comparative analyses of Chinese and Western cohorts.
authors: Zhou C, Sun C, Jin H et al.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Microsatellite instability (MSI) is a pivotal pan-cancer biomarker for immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. However, due to the low frequency of MSI-high (MSI-H) in lung cancer (LC), the genetic characteristics and prognosis of this subgroup were rarely reported.
METHODS: A total of 4539 Chinese LC patients were screened for microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H)/deficient DNA mismatch repair (dMMR) status. Of these, 344 patients with available detailed clinical and genomic data were further analyzed to assess clinicopathologic correlates and genomic differences compared to 1053 samples from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Comparative analyses were performed between MSI-H/dMMR and microsatellite stable (MSS)/proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) groups, as well as between the Chinese and TCGA dMMR cohorts. Additionally, we performed a systematic literature review to evaluate clinical outcomes.
RESULTS: We observed an overall MSI-H/dMMR prevalence of 1.08% in Chinese patients. While the rate in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) was 1.94%, the phenotype was predominantly observed in lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC, 3.81%), which was approximately four-fold higher than that in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD, 0.89%). TCGA data showed similar LUSC predominance (1.85% vs. 1.41% in LUAD). MSI-H/dMMR status were correlated with younger age, early-stage, and non-metastatic disease. Chinese MSI-H/dMMR LC samples showed frequent TP53, EGFR, and BRCA2 mutations, enriched indel mutations and C>T transitions. TCGA MSI-H/dMMR tumors had higher TP53 (82.4% vs. 52.3%) and lower EGFR mutations than Chinese patients. A literature review of 16 MSI-H/dMMR patients suggests prolonged progression-free survival (PFS) with ICI regimens.
CONCLUSIONS: MSI-H/dMMR LC exhibits distinct clinicogenomic features between Chinese vs. TCGA population, with histotype- and cohort-specific mutational landscapes. These findings inform MMR-driven tumor biology and ethnic-dependent therapeutic strategies.

title: A Clinical Study Comparing the Efficacy and Safety of Befotertinib Versus Icotinib in Patients With Previously Untreated EGFR-sensitive Mutation-positive Non-small Cell Lung Cancer With ECOG Score ≥2
conditions: Locally Advanced or Metastatic Non-small Cell Lung Cancer With Previously Untreated EGFR-sensitive Mutations and ECOG Performance Status Score ≥2
summary: This study is a multicenter, randomized, open-label, parallel-controlled clinical trial. It is designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Befotertinib versus Icotinib as first-line treatment in patients with previously untreated EGFR-sensitive mutation-positive locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer with ECOG score ≥2.

title: KEYNOTE-867: A Phase III, Randomized, Double-Blind Study of Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy With Pembrolizumab for Unresected Stage I or II Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
authors: Jabbour SK, Sótér S, Eaton M et al.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) is standard of care for inoperable stage I or II non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). KEYNOTE-867 (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03924869) evaluated the addition of pembrolizumab to SBRT in participants diagnosed with stage I or II NSCLC that was inoperable or in participants who refused surgery.
METHODS: Adults with untreated, stage I or II (T1 to limited T3, N0, M0) NSCLC (AJCC 8th edition) that was inoperable, or adults who refused surgery, were randomly assigned 1:1 to thoracic SBRT to primary tumors for ≤2 weeks concomitantly with pembrolizumab 200 mg or placebo once every 3 weeks for ≤17 cycles. The primary end point was event-free survival (EFS) by blinded independent central review.
RESULTS: A total of 448 participants were randomly assigned to SBRT plus pembrolizumab (n = 227) or SBRT plus placebo (n = 221). The median time from random assignment to the data cutoff date (June 11, 2024) for the prespecified first interim analysis was 20.6 (range, 1.3-56.8) months. The median EFS (95% CI) was 31.2 (22.5 to 39.1) months and 28.3 (19.8 to 33.1) months for the pembrolizumab and placebo arms, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.69 to 1.24]; P = .2932). Among participants who received ≥1 dose of study treatment, grade 3-5 treatment-related adverse events (AEs) occurred in 46/226 (20.4%) participants in the pembrolizumab arm and 8/218 (3.7%) participants in the placebo arm. There were five treatment-related deaths all of which occurred in the pembrolizumab arm (2.2%).
CONCLUSION: The addition of pembrolizumab to SBRT did not improve EFS and was associated with a higher incidence of treatment-related AEs compared with SBRT alone in participants with inoperable stage I or II NSCLC. Based on the benefit-risk profile, the KEYNOTE-867 trial was prematurely stopped, and all study treatment was discontinued.

title: Economic evaluation of six immune checkpoint inhibitor-based first-line therapies for advanced squamous non-small-cell lung cancer: a cost-effectiveness analysis based on network meta-analysis.
authors: Qiu Z, Wang G, Lou Y et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advanced squamous non-small-cell lung cancer (sq-NSCLC) imposes a substantial clinical and economic burden. Immune checkpoint inhibitors (sugemalimab, tislelizumab, penpulimab, serplulimab, camrelizumab, and pembrolizumab) combined with chemotherapy improve survival, but their comparative cost-effectiveness remains uncertain.
METHODS: A three-state partitioned survival model with 3-week cycles and a lifetime horizon was developed from the Chinese healthcare-system perspective. Clinical efficacy was derived from six phase 3 trials and synthesized using network meta-analysis. Costs, life-years (LYs), quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), and incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) for each ICI-based regimen versus chemotherapy were estimated. The willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold was set at $27,906/QALY. Deterministic, probabilistic, scenario, and full incremental analyses were performed.
RESULTS: In the base-case analysis, chemotherapy alone yielded 0.71 QALYs at $12,227.47. All ICI-based regimens increased QALYs to between 1.24 and 2.07. Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy provided the greatest health benefit, yielding 2.07 QALYs, but had an ICER of $70,913.04 per QALY versus chemotherapy alone. Penpulimab plus chemotherapy had the lowest ICER versus chemotherapy alone ($13,064.23 per QALY), followed by camrelizumab ($13,361.50/QALY), and tislelizumab plus chemotherapy ($14,022.95/QALY), all below the WTP threshold. Sugemalimab plus chemotherapy and serplulimab plus chemotherapy exceeded the threshold. Probabilistic sensitivity analysis indicated that camrelizumab plus chemotherapy had the highest probability of being cost-effective (95%) at $27,906/QALY. In the full incremental analysis, the efficiency frontier comprised chemotherapy alone, penpulimab plus chemotherapy, camrelizumab plus chemotherapy, and pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy; camrelizumab plus chemotherapy was the preferred strategy after dominated options were excluded.
CONCLUSION: At the selected WTP threshold, camrelizumab plus chemotherapy may be the preferred first-line strategy after strictly and extendedly dominated alternatives were excluded. This finding depends on the indirect comparisons, chemotherapy baseline, drug prices, survival extrapolation, and post-progression assumptions.

title: GlycoRNA-related cellular program scoring identifies Siglec- and myeloid-associated tumor microenvironments for glycoRNA validation.
authors: Kong M, Guan X, Jing Y et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glycosylated RNAs (glycoRNAs) represent a recently recognized connection between RNA biology and cell-surface glycobiology. However, whether glycoRNA-related processes are relevant to human tumors remains unclear, partly because direct glycoRNA measurements are not yet available across large cancer cohorts. We therefore used transcriptomic data to identify tumor settings in which glycoRNA-related programs may be most suitable for further experimental validation.
METHODS: We curated a glycoRNA-focused literature evidence base and manually reviewed the top extracted relations to define gene modules related to RNA identity, N-glycan and sialylation pathways, RNA trafficking, and lectin/Siglec recognition. The glycoRNA-related cellular program score is an expression-based composite score representing coordinated glycoRNA-related cellular programs, including RNA processing, glycan biosynthesis, trafficking, and lectin/Siglec recognition. It is designed to prioritize tumor contexts for experimental glycoRNA validation. The score was applied to 9,186 TCGA tumors from 32 cancer types and analyzed together with clinical variables, leukocyte fraction, immune signatures, Siglec/checkpoint/myeloid-axis scores, and non-overlapping sensitivity models. Glioblastoma single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets were used for additional context-level validation.
RESULTS: Higher glycoRNA-related cellular program scores were observed in several tumor types, including stomach adenocarcinoma, glioblastoma, lung adenocarcinoma, esophageal carcinoma, mesothelioma, pancreatic adenocarcinoma, breast cancer, and lung squamous carcinoma. Survival analyses did not show robust FDR-significant associations after adjustment for age, sex, stage, and tumor type, suggesting that the score should not be interpreted as a general prognostic biomarker. In sensitivity analyses that removed immune and Siglec-related genes from the predictor, the score remained associated with Siglec-decoder, myeloid, checkpoint, and integrated niche features after adjustment for leukocyte fraction and cancer-type effects. Within-cancer meta-analysis supported these associations across cancer types, although effect sizes varied. In glioblastoma, higher scores were found in tumor, myeloid, mesenchymal, and niche-associated compartments in single-cell and spatial analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: This study presents an expression-based map of glycoRNA-related cellular program across human cancers. The results suggest that glycoRNA-related transcriptional programs tend to occur in immune- and myeloid-enriched tumor microenvironments, particularly those involving Siglec-associated features. These findings prioritize tumor contexts for biochemical, imaging, spatial, and perturbation-based glycoRNA validation.

title: Real-World Experience With Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Natural Language Processing for Identification and Management of Incidental Lung Nodules.
authors: Ploucher S, Nguyen AD, Altaf R et al.
abstract: BackgroundIncidental lung nodules (ILNs) are common, but adherence to guideline-recommended follow-up is variable, which may contribute to delayed diagnosis of malignancy. Artificial intelligence (AI) platforms using natural language processing (NLP) may improve identification, but their impact on clinical management and outcomes remains uncertain.ObjectivesThis study describes ILN identification, follow-up management, and timeliness of cancer treatment after implementation of an AI-enabled NLP platform at a large health system.DesignSingle-center retrospective observational study.MethodsAdults with ILNs identified on imaging between April 2023 and May 2024 were included. The pre-AI cohort was identified using diagnosis codes, while the post-AI cohort was identified using an NLP-based AI platform. Because these methods captured different populations, no formal comparative testing was performed, and outcomes were summarized descriptively.ResultsA total of 1,098 patients with ILNs were identified: 228 from 6,828 pre-AI imaging studies (3.3%) and 870 from 9,902 post-AI imaging studies (8.8%). Most pre-AI ILNs were identified on outpatient imaging (74%), while post-AI ILNs were identified in inpatient (35%), emergency department (26%), and outpatient (39%) settings. A follow-up recommendation was documented for 195 of 228 pre-AI patients (85.5%) and 563 of 870 post-AI patients (64.7%). Among these patients, completion was documented for 167 of 195 (85.6%) and 414 of 563 (73.5%), respectively. Malignancy was documented in 28 of 228 pre-AI patients (12.3%) and 15 of 870 post-AI patients (1.7%). Median imaging-to-biopsy time was 78 days pre-AI and 120 days post-AI; biopsy-to-treatment and imaging-to-treatment intervals were similar.ConclusionThe post-AI cohort included more identified ILNs and a greater proportion from acute-care settings than the historical pre-AI cohort. Because identification methods were not comparable, observed differences in documented malignancy diagnosis and treatment timing cannot be attributed to the platform. Effective implementation requires defined clinical ownership and follow-up infrastructure.

title: Venous Thromboembolism Reporting in Fusion-Positive NSCLC Treated with Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: A Systematic Review of Safety Reporting and Protocol-Level Provisions in Phase I-IV Clinical Trials.
authors: Citarella F, Fiorenti M, Fragale C et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant complication in patients with fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the completeness and consistency of thromboembolic safety reporting in clinical trials of tyrosine kinase inhibitors remain poorly characterized.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review of phase I-IV clinical trials evaluating targeted therapies in fusion-positive NSCLC. Protocols, publications, and online trial registry updates were systematically reviewed to assess thromboembolic event ascertainment, reporting practices, protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions, and VTE-related eligibility criteria.
RESULTS: A total of 108 reporting sources from 61 study entries (58 unique trials) were reviewed. Pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis were the predominant reported events. VTE-related information was highly fragmented across reporting sources: 14 study entries reported events exclusively through full-text publications, 19 exclusively through online trial updates, and 15 through both sources. Study protocols rarely prespecified thromboembolic events as dedicated safety outcomes, more commonly addressing them in eligibility criteria, anticoagulant therapy provisions, or differential diagnosis guidance. More than 40% of study entries lacked protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions and nearly 60% lacked VTE-related eligibility restrictions. Marked heterogeneity was observed in event definitions, reporting practices, safety ascertainment, and observation periods.
CONCLUSIONS: In fusion-positive NSCLC trials, heterogeneity in event ascertainment and reporting, rather than a true scarcity of thromboembolic events, represents a major limitation of the available evidence. Greater standardization of safety reporting and integration of trial registry and publication data may improve the completeness, comparability, and interpretability of future studies.

title: [Diagnosis and Treatment of COPD: A Guideline for Respiratory Specialists 2026].
authors: Kahnert K, Abdo M, Alter P et al.
abstract: This S2k guideline updates the recommendations for the diagnosis and treatment of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) by respiratory specialists and complements the German National Disease Management Guideline (NVL) with specialist recommendations for diagnosis and treatment. The guideline is based on current scientific evidence and a structured interdisciplinary S2k consensus process involving numerous scientific societies. Major updates include recognition of COPD as a heterogeneous disease, with expanded recommendations on its etiopathogenesis, early detection, and contemporary diagnostic approaches, including biomarkers, thoracic computed tomography, and lung cancer screening, as well as updated risk stratification. Recommendations on smoking cessation, non-pharmacological management, and pharmacological treatment have been comprehensively revised. These include consistent use of dual bronchodilation, earlier implementation of inhaled triple therapy in appropriate patients, and consideration of emerging treatment options, including biologics. Additional updates address the management of comorbidities, interventional treatment of advanced emphysema, and inpatient management of acute COPD exacerbations. The guideline aims to support individualized, phenotype-oriented, and evidence-based care for patients with COPD.

title: Neoadjuvant and perioperative chemoimmunotherapy versus chemotherapy for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Zhu T, Zhou J, Liu D et al.
abstract: Although neoadjuvant and perioperative chemoimmunotherapy improve outcomes in resectable non-small-cell lung cancer, treatment effects remain incompletely defined for specific subgroups. We searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science through 3 December 2025 and pooled eight randomized trials involving 3387 patients using random-effects models. Exploratory event-free survival (EFS) analyses yielded hazard ratios (HRs) of 0.57 for perioperative and 0.66 for pure neoadjuvant regimens versus chemotherapy. The indirect ratio of HRs was 0.86 (95% CI, 0.63-1.18; interaction P = 0.347), with insufficient precision to establish equivalence. Among patients with PD-L1 tumor-cell expression <1%, the pooled EFS HR was 0.77 (95% CI, 0.65-0.91), although all six trial-specific CIs included 1. China-only trials had numerically lower EFS HRs than international trials (0.48 versus 0.63; interaction P = 0.053). Surgery occurred in 82.2% versus 77.9% (risk ratio, 1.06; risk difference, 4.7 percentage points); nominal significance varied with study omission. Overall EFS and overall survival favored chemoimmunotherapy (HRs, 0.59 [95% CI,0.52-0.66] and 0.68 [0.57-0.80], respectively). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events increased in the two eligible perioperative trials (risk ratio, 1.12; 95% CI, 1.02-1.24). Trial-level pathological response-survival analyses did not establish surrogate validity. Subgroup findings remain hypothesis-generating, and the surgical difference does not establish a clinically meaningful improvement in resectability.

title: Clinical outcomes of COPD associated with cigarette smoke, biomass smoke, and combined exposure: A retrospective observational study.
authors: Yüksel A, Esendağlı D, Nezalzova P et al.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) related to combined exposure to cigarette and biomass smoke is insufficiently characterized. The aim of this study was to compare exacerbations and chronic respiratory failure (CRF) across smoking-associated, biomass-associated, and combined exposure COPD.
METHODS: In this retrospective, multicenter, observational study, 319 patients with stable COPD were classified into three groups based on exposure history: smoking-associated (n=159), biomass-associated (n=80), and combined cigarette and biomass exposure (n=80). Smoking and biomass exposure histories were retrospectively obtained from medical records. Cigarette exposure was quantified in pack-years, biomass exposure was assessed according to the documented type and duration of household fuel use, and patients with both exposures were classified as the combined-exposure group. Exacerbation frequency, CRF, and pulmonary function tests were evaluated. Multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, cardiac diseases, sarcopenia, and lung cancer were used to assess the associations of exposure group with annual exacerbation frequency and CRF.
RESULTS: Patients with combined exposure were younger (59.22 ± 10.82 years) compared with those in the smoking-associated (61.37 ± 11.04 years) and biomass-associated groups (63.45 ± 11.92 years, p=0.015). The combined exposure group had lower FEV1 (% predicted: 48.27 ± 10.14 vs 55.28 ± 17.61 and 55.62 ± 11.29; p=0.003) and higher dyspnea scores (mMRC: 2.18 vs 1.39 and 1.88; p<0.001). Exacerbation burden was significantly greater in the combined exposure group, including higher annual exacerbation rates (2.18 ± 0.82 vs 2.08 ± 0.22 and 1.88 ± 0.32; p=0.041) and severe exacerbations (1.78 ± 0.35 vs 1.39 ± 0.18 and 1.20 ± 0.19; p<0.001). CRF was more frequent in the combined-exposure group (26.2% vs 17.0% and 11.2%; p=0.028). In adjusted analyses, combined exposure was independently associated with increased risk of severe exacerbations compared with cigarette smoking alone (AOR=1.89; 95% CI: 1.22-2.96).
CONCLUSIONS: Findings of this study suggest that combined exposure to cigarette and biomass smoke is potentially associated with earlier COPD presentation, increased exacerbation frequency and lower FEV1.

title: Latent Transition Analysis of Symptom Burden Before and After Pulmonary Rehabilitation in Postoperative Lung Cancer Patients.
authors: Wu Y, Yang Q, Wang J et al.
abstract:
AIM: To identify latent classes of symptom burden in lung cancer patients before and after pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) and to examine factors associated with transitions between classes.
DESIGN: A longitudinal study.
METHODS: The M. D. Anderson Symptom Inventory (Chinese version) was completed by 273 postoperative lung cancer patients before (T1) and 12 weeks after PR (T2). Latent profile analysis identified symptom burden classes, and latent transition analysis estimated the probability of moving between classes. Measurement invariance was tested, and the two-class solution was retained on the basis of fit indices, entropy and interpretability. Univariate-significant variables entered a logistic regression model.
RESULTS: Two latent classes were identified at both T1 and T2 (high and low symptom burden). The two-class solution was retained because it showed the lowest AIC, BIC and aBIC, adequate entropy (0.844 at T1; 0.902 at T2) and interpretable profiles, whereas the three-class model did not improve fit and yielded small classes. Among 262 patients (95.97% valid), the low burden class was stable (0.863), and 61.07% of patients in the high burden class at T1 moved to the low burden class at T2; these probabilities denote the proportion of patients moving between classes. Age <45 years (OR = 2.345), no financial burden (OR = 2.841), satisfactory sleep (OR = 3.130) and family living (OR = 2.949) were associated with transition from the high to the low burden class, whereas age ≥60 years (OR = 0.724), unmarried (OR = 0.418) and divorced (OR = 0.405) status with lower odds of transition.
CONCLUSION: Symptom burden in postoperative lung cancer patients is heterogeneous and follows class-specific trajectories. Younger age, better sleep and stronger family and financial resources were associated with a favourable transition. As this was a single-arm observational study, the findings indicate associations rather than causal effects of PR.

title: Risk factors for venous thromboembolic events at 90 days in hospitalized patients with advanced cancer receiving palliative care: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
authors: Luna-Benitez MC, Benavides-Cruz J, Borda-Restrepo DC et al.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Evidence regarding venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk in palliative care populations remains scarce, and current thromboprophylaxis recommendations are largely extrapolated from non-palliative oncology cohorts. This study aimed to determine the 90-day incidence of VTE and associated clinical risk factors in hospitalized patients with advanced cancer receiving palliative care.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included adults with advanced cancer enrolled in a palliative care program who were hospitalized between 2018 and 2024 at two tertiary care centers in Bogotá, Colombia. VTE incidence was calculated, and clinical risk factors were identified using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: A total of 782 patients were included (mean age 61 years; 58.7% male). Withing 90 days of admission, 81 patients (10.3%) developed VTE, corresponding to an incidence density of 2.3 events per 1,000 patient-days. Pulmonary embolism accounted for 40.7% of VTE events. In the adjusted analysis, lung cancer was associated with an increased risk of VTE (HR 2.34; p = 0.010), whereas higher Karnofsky Performance Status was associated with a lower risk (HR 0.98; p = 0.020). Age, sex, body mass index, baseline hemoglobin, active anticancer treatment, and white blood cell count were not independently associated with VTE. Overall, 90-day mortality was 66.3%.
CONCLUSION: VTE was a frequent complication among hospitalized patients with advanced cancer receiving palliative care. Lung cancer and poor functional status were independently associated with VTE, whereas traditional clinical predictors were not associated with VTE. These findings support individualized VTE risk assessment and highlight the need for future prospective studies evaluating thromboprophylaxis strategies in palliative care settings.

title: Exploring the Nutritional Experiences of Lung Cancer Patients Undergoing Chemotherapy: A Qualitative Study.
authors: Liu S, Fu ZW, Xiong YW et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Malnutrition is highly prevalent among patients with lung cancer undergoing chemotherapy; however, its management remains delayed. A comprehensive understanding of patients' subjective perceptions of their nutritional experience is vital for delivering patient-centered nutritional care. This study aimed to explore the nutritional changes and nutritional support needs of patients with lung cancer undergoing chemotherapy using a descriptive qualitative approach.
METHODS: Qualitative interviews were conducted with 22 patients with lung cancer undergoing chemotherapy. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis, guided by the principles of Consensual Qualitative Research. The reporting of this study strictly adhered to the Standards for Reporting Qualitative Research.
RESULTS: Twenty-two participants completed the interviews, ranging in age from 51 to 76 years; 3 were female, and 19 were male. Analysis revealed a thematic framework of nutritional experiences comprising four themes: diverse appetite change trajectories; complex dilemmas in nutritional management; gradual development of nutritional adjustment strategies; and an urgent need for professional nutritional management.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study provides evidence of three main appetite-change patterns among patients with lung cancer undergoing chemotherapy: fluctuating, stable, and continuously declining. Patients may experience major nutritional challenges but gradually develop coping strategies after several chemotherapy cycles. Establishing a multidisciplinary team and fully developing the role of nurses to provide continuous nutritional management is key to alleviating nutrition-related symptoms throughout treatment.
IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING PRACTICE: This study helps nurses understand patients' experiences of nutritional changes from a dynamic perspective and their nutritional needs. As gatekeepers of patients' health, nurses have an urgent need for interdisciplinary training in nutritional management, which may provide valuable insights for the nutritional management of future patients with lung cancer undergoing chemotherapy.

title: Metformin Attenuates Glucose-Driven Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression by Targeting GPD2-Mediated Metabolic Plasticity.
authors: Siripongsampan S, Kateyai M, Piriyapairoje K et al.
abstract: Glucose metabolism is crucial for cancer cell survival and proliferation. Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells exhibit distinct metabolic adaptations that support tumor progression under nutrient-limited conditions. The study examines the impact of glucose availability and GPD2-mediated metabolic adaptation on HCC progression, as well as how these processes are modulated by glucose transport inhibitors and metformin. Cell proliferation and migration of HCC cells (HepG2 and Huh7) and lung cancer cells (A549) were examined under different glucose concentrations using MTT, colony formation, and scratch assays. The impacts of glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1) inhibitors and metformin were also evaluated. Gene and protein expression data were analyzed from TCGA/CPTAC datasets, and GPD2 expression was validated by immunohistochemistry. High glucose enhanced proliferation and migration of liver cancer cells. Unlike A549, HepG2 and Huh7 cells maintained growth under glucose deprivation, indicating metabolic plasticity. GPD2 was markedly upregulated in HCC tissues and correlated with poor survival. Metformin suppressed cell proliferation and migration in a dose-dependent manner, with stronger effects under low-glucose conditions. Mechanistically, metformin downregulated Cyclin D1 and XIAP, induced Caspase-3 cleavage, and reduced the EMT marker, Slug. Correlation analyses revealed positive associations between GPD2 and CCND1 or SNAI2, indicating a link between GPD2 and cell cycle and EMT signaling. In conclusion, HCC cells utilize GPD2-mediated metabolic adaptation to sustain growth under glucose-limiting conditions. GPD2 represents a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in HCC. Metformin effectively inhibits HCC progression by disrupting GPD2-linked pro-survival and EMT pathways.

title: Positive Impact of Hypertension in Patients with Early-stage Lung Cancer Treated With Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy.
authors: Lim JH, Jang JH, Lee J et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: This study aimed to analyze the effect of hypertension on recurrence and progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with early-stage lung cancer who underwent curative stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This study included 100 patients with T1-T3N0M0 lung cancer who underwent lung SBRT using CyberKnife or volumetric-modulated arc therapy at Inha University Hospital between July 2008 and June 2025. Recurrence rates and PFS were analyzed. Data on hypertension and specific types of antihypertensive medications were retrospectively reviewed from electronic medical records.
RESULTS: The median follow-up period was 31.0 months (range=0.7-136.7 months). Of the 100 patients, 52 had hypertension. Recurrence occurred in 38 patients, including 25 with locoregional failure and 13 with distant metastases. Recurrence rates were significantly lower in patients with hypertension (p=0.015), with reduced locoregional recurrence (p=0.022), whereas distant metastasis showed no significant correlation with hypertension (p=0.315). Hypertensive drug users (n=37) had lower recurrence rates (p=0.003). Recurrence was higher in male patients (p=0.049) and lower in those aged >70 years (p=0.033). Patients with hypertension showed significantly improved PFS (p=0.010) but no difference in overall survival based on hypertension status (p=0.319). Other factors that positively affected PFS included female sex and age >70 years. Patients actively receiving antihypertensive medication showed greater PFS than those who did not (p=0.016). In particular, those using beta-blockers showed a low recurrence rate (0%, p=0.033).
CONCLUSION: The therapeutic effects of lung SBRT appear more pronounced in patients with hypertension. This favorable outcome may be related to the administration of antihypertensive medications, suggesting the need for further investigation into the underlying mechanisms.

title: Brain-sensing synNotch-CAR T cells enable precise targeting and clearance of diffuse midline glioma in multiple preclinical models.
authors: Lakshmanachetty S, Simic MS, Watchmaker PB et al.
abstract: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) is a lethal pediatric brain tumor with limited therapeutic options and a poor prognosis. The success of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy requires both improving T cell tumor infiltration and persistence and reducing the risk of on-target/off-tumor toxicity. Here, we adapted and advanced a brain-restricted CAR T cell platform previously validated in glioblastoma to address the anatomical and biological challenges of DMG. We engineered a T cell circuit in which a brain-specific synthetic Notch (synNotch) receptor recognizing brevican (BCAN) induced CAR expression against EphA2 or IL-13Rα2 ("B-SYNC"), thereby restricting CAR expression to the central nervous system (CNS). In immunodeficient DMG models, a single infusion of intravenous (iv) or intracerebroventricular (icv) B-SYNC circuit T cells led to tumor infiltration, sustained persistence, antitumor activity, and extended survival. An alternative BCAN-primed CAR targeting B7-H3 or IL-13Rα2 ("B-SYNC-B/I") similarly improved therapeutic efficacy when delivered intravenously. However, icv administration triggered fatal neurotoxicity because of low-level B7-H3 expression in nontumor CNS regions, indicating that rapid CNS exposure via icv delivery can amplify off-tumor toxicity. In contrast, in an immunocompetent syngeneic DMG model, both iv and icv delivery of a murinized BCAN-gated B7-H3 CAR (mB-SYNC-B7-H3) achieved durable tumor clearance and resistance to rechallenge without any detectable neurotoxicity. Mechanistically, synNotch-primed CAR T cells exhibited reduced exhaustion, enhanced activation, and enrichment of naïve and stem cell memory-like subsets. These findings demonstrate that brain-sensing synNotch CAR T circuits represent a generalizable and translatable strategy for targeting multiple CNS malignancies, including DMG.

title: Frontier therapeutic strategies and molecular mechanisms of glioblastoma (Review).
authors: Shao L, Sun S, Yang L et al.
abstract: The present study critically summarizes recent progress in therapeutic strategies and molecular mechanisms of glioblastoma (GBM) from 2020 to 2025, appraise the strength of evidence underlying emerging treatments, and provide practical references for individualized clinical decision-making. Relevant studies were retrieved from PubMed, Embase and Web of Science using predefined search strings combining 'glioblastoma', 'molecular classification', 'targeted therapy', 'immunotherapy' and 'drug resistance'. After duplicate removal and independent two-reviewer screening, 86 studies were included and synthesized, and the evidence was graded according to study design (randomized trials vs. single-arm early-phase trials vs. preclinical studies). The results demonstrated that molecular classification centered on IDH mutation and MGMT promoter methylation has become the basis of GBM treatment decision-making, although the WHO CNS5 classification now integrates additional diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers (for example, CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion, EGFR amplification, TERT promoter mutation, chromosome 7 gain/10 loss). 5-aminolevulinic acid fluorescence-guided surgery improves the extent of resection, and tumor treating fields provide an additional survival benefit in newly diagnosed GBM. Emerging approaches, including dual-target CAR-T cells, mRNA vaccines and metabolic inhibitors, have shown preliminary signals of activity in recurrent GBM, but most remain investigational and are supported by early-phase trials with small sample sizes. GBM treatment resistance arises from interconnected DNA repair, epigenetic, metabolic, tumor microenvironment and glioblastoma stem cell networks. In conclusion, GBM management is transitioning from empirical therapy toward molecularly guided precision therapy, but the translational gap between promising preclinical findings and proven clinical benefit remains substantial. Multimodal strategies integrating refined molecular classification, blood-brain barrier-penetrant drug delivery and rationally combined, rigorously tested therapies represent the most realistic path to improving GBM outcomes.

title: Antibody‒cell conjugates: A novel "off-the-shelf" modality bridging ADCs and CAR-T for cancer immunotherapy.
authors: Dai Y, Xie Y, Ma X et al.
abstract: Antibody‒cell conjugates (ACCs) represent a promising therapeutic strategy emerging in the biopharmaceutical industry to overcome the limitations of current immunotherapies. ACCs constitute a novel class of living drugs developed by anchoring functional antibodies onto the surface of living cells via specific linkers or conjugation methods. These carrier cells encompass both immune effector cells (such as Natural Killer cells, γδ T cells, and activated T cells) and non-immune cells (such as erythrocytes and platelets). Distinct from genetic engineering, ACCs directly modify the cell surface using chemical biology, enzymatic catalysis, or physical assembly, thereby endowing cells with precise tumor-targeting capabilities while preserving their intrinsic biological functions. This technology facilitates the scalable production of "off-the-shelf" therapeutics and has shown promising potential in treating both hematological malignancies and refractory solid tumors with a superior safety profile. This review systematically examines the current construction strategies and carrier cell selection for ACCs, covering both immune effector cells and non-immune carrier cells, and discusses the clinical progress, key challenges, and future directions.

title: Engineering next-generation CAR-NK cells for hematological malignancies: genome editing, synthetic biology, and precision immunotherapy.
authors: Bahr AR, Basem Y, Alhejely A et al.
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-based immunotherapy has transformed cancer treatment by enabling engineered immune cells to selectively recognize and eliminate malignant targets, with CAR-T cells establishing the first major clinical success in this field. However, severe associated toxicities, logistical complexities of autologous manufacturing, and high rates of antigen-loss relapse have accelerated the development of alternative effector platforms such as CAR-NK cells. CAR-NK cells combine antigen-directed cytotoxicity with the innate antitumor functions of natural killer cells, offering a potentially safer and more readily available off-the-shelf therapeutic strategy. Nevertheless, the clinical efficacy of CAR-NK therapy is constrained by key biological and translational hurdles: brief in vivo persistence, inadequate trafficking and solid tumor infiltration, severe susceptibility to tumor microenvironment-mediated immunosuppression, and antigen escape driven by tumor heterogeneity. These biological constraints are compounded by technical bottlenecks, including cell source variability, limited large-scale expansion capacity, ex vivo functional exhaustion, and an absence of standardized manufacturing protocols. To address these multi-faceted barriers, recent advances in genome engineering, systems biology, and computational modeling provide promising routes forward. Given that prolonged exposure to immunosuppressive niches induces functional impairment, genome-editing strategies targeting inhibitory checkpoints and persistence programs are crucial; however, enhancing persistence requires stringent safeguards to mitigate toxicity risks from constitutive signaling or genomic instability. Thus, engineering next-generation CAR-NK cells necessitates balancing extended longevity, potent cytotoxicity, and safety. Multiomics approaches facilitate deeper characterization of CAR-NK functional states and tumor-immune interactions, whereas artificial intelligence-guided engineering integrates high-dimensional biological and manufacturing data to optimize receptor design, predict therapeutic performance, and accelerate translational workflows. Collectively, these innovations support a paradigm shift toward programmable CAR-NK cells that can dynamically sense, adapt, and respond to tumor evolution, driving the transition toward autonomous, highly scalable, and precisely controllable cellular immunotherapies in precision oncology.

title: Tumor Associated Neutrophils Extend NETs To Spatially Drive Necroptosis In Glioblastoma
summary: Background: Glioblastoma is pathologically characterized by extensive pseudopalisading necrosis, a hallmark linked to therapeutic resistance and dismal prognosis. While traditionally viewed as a passive ischemic event, the precise radiogenomic drivers and spatial immune architectures orchestrating active tumor necrosis remain poorly understood. Methods: We integrated macroscopic clinical MRI radiomics with public genomic datasets (n=3,639), single-cell spatial transcriptomics, and high-resolution protein immunofluorescence (IF) assays in a novel co-mutant murine model to map the necrotic microenvironment. Results: Radiomic analysis of patient MRIs demonstrated that high tumoral necrotic volume serves as a powerful independent biomarker for poor long-term survival. This macro-structural necrosis phenotype is radiogenomically driven by cell-intrinsic TP53, PTEN, and NF1 (PPN) co-mutations. Spatial transcriptomic profiling of PPN-deficient tumors revealed distinct cellular topography, separating a proliferative, invasive niche (EGFR+ SOX+, TypeInv) from a hyper-aggressive necrotic niche (ERBB3+, TypeNec). Mechanistically, TypeNec cells deploy a prominent CCL5/CXCL2 chemokine milieu that actively recruits and prompts tumor-associated neutrophils to undergo neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation. This overactive neutrophil infiltrate drives a feed-forward loop of intrinsic tumor necroptosis mediated by the release of the damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) protein HMGB2. This cascade could be therapeutically dismantled using targeted anti-inflammatory compounds. Finally, multi-cohort clinical validation confirmed that an HMGB2high signature dictates a high-risk, myeloid-rich immunosuppressive microenvironment in glioblastoma patients. Conclusions: Our findings redefine glioblastoma necrosis as an active, mutation-driven immunopathological process. The HMGB2-mediated DAMP necroptosis cascade and associated myeloid chemokines provide robust prognostic biomark

title: Quantifying Localized Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocytes by Deep Learning on H&E Images: Analytical Validation and Prognostic Value in Lung Adenocarcinoma
summary: Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) are a critical determinant of response to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). However, assessing the clinical utility of TIL quantification is challenging due to subjective manual scoring and differences in methodology, including some that may obscure localized immune responses critical to ICI response. Together, these issues limit our understanding of potential prognostic benefits of performing routine TIL quantification. Here, we present the "focal TIL score", an artificial intelligence-powered biomarker derived from routinely generated Hematoxylin & Eosin (H&E) pathology images which measures TIL density within tiles across the entire relevant tissue region in order to account for spatial heterogeneity of localized lymphocytic infiltration. Underlying this method are two deep learning models that ensure accurate, reproducible, and interpretable quantification: one for lymphocyte detection trained on IHC-derived ground truth, and one for segmentation of tumor and tumor-adjacent stroma region ("scorable region") trained on consensus pathologist annotations. We performed an analytical validation of the two models, demonstrating high overall performance: lymphocyte model concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) = 0.90, scorable region model Dice score = 0.87. We then performed a prognostic association study in a cohort of 685 ICI-treated LUAD patients and saw that, the focal TIL score was significantly associated with overall survival (HR=0.60, 95% CI 0.48-0.75, P<0.001), outperforming the standard biomarker PD-L1. Our findings show that quantifying the spatial intensity of immune infiltration, rather than the global average, provides a superior measure of the anti-tumor immune response. The accessibility and standardization associated with this approach may enable further studies and developments in precision oncology for LUAD.

title: Histone modifications define distinct nucleosome positions in cell-free DNA
summary: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentation patterns reflect nucleosome positioning. We asked whether variation in nucleosome positions in cfDNA can reveal chromatin states and associated histone modifications. Using cell-free chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (cfChIP-seq) in plasma from patients with prostate cancer, we identified 35,120 modification-associated positions (MAPs), loci where nucleosomes bearing active (H3K4me2) and repressive (H3K9me3) histone marks occupy reproducibly offset positions. These offsets recurred across histone marks, an independent cfChIP-seq cohort, and nuclease-digested chromatin from cell lines. MAPs were enriched in transcribed genes but depleted near transcription start sites and CTCF-binding sites where nucleosome positioning is constrained. Across 2,535 cfDNA sequencing datasets, nucleosome protection at a subset of MAPs correlated with tumor fraction (TF), reflecting differences in histone modification status between cancer-derived and non-malignant chromatin. In targeted sequencing panels, a 50-MAP model using fragments from < 0.001% of the genome distinguished samples with tumor fractions [≥]3% vs 0% (AUCs = 0.91-0.96 across prostate, breast, and lung cancers) and outperformed a state-of-the-art fragmentomics-based tumor fraction predictor. MAP-derived estimates correlated with reference TFs (r = 0.89) and longitudinal changes in TF (r = 0.91). MAP protection at ASCL1 binding sites identified neuroendocrine transformation of prostate cancer from cfDNA. These findings establish histone-modification-associated nucleosome positioning as a mutation-independent readout of tumor fraction and cancer state from routine cfDNA sequencing.

title: Pulmonary colonization of Candida albicans drives breast cancer lung metastasis via candidalysin
summary: The intratumoral mycobiome is emerging as a key modulator of cancer progression, with specific fungal taxa as potential biomarkers. However, whether and how mycobiomes colonizing distant organs contribute to tumor evolution remains largely unexplored. Here, we identify selective enrichment of Candida albicans in breast cancer lung metastases. Mechanistically, the fungal virulence factor candidalysin activates pulmonary mast cells, which release chemotactic mediators that expand immunosuppressive populations and suppress cytotoxic lymphocyte activity, remodeling the lung into a metastasis-permissive microenvironment. Analysis of clinical isolates and isogenic mutants further demonstrates that candidalysin secretion levels dictate metastasis-promoting potential. Informed by these findings, we developed a combination regimen that concurrently eliminates fungal colonization, stabilizes mast cells, and reverses the immunosuppressive microenvironment, thereby significantly curtailing metastatic progression. Collectively, our study establishes pulmonary C. albicans colonization as a driver of breast cancer lung metastasis and provides a mechanistic framework for targeting mycobiome-host interactions in metastatic disease.

title: Neuroendocrine Differentiation Mediates Escape from HER2-Targeted Therapy in Breast Cancer.
authors: Würth R, Cheytan T, Schwerd-Kleine P et al.
abstract: Neuroendocrine differentiation (NED) promotes lineage plasticity and therapy resistance in prostate and lung cancers. Here we identify NED as a route of treatment escape in breast cancer: neuroendocrine features emerged or increased in 22% of progressive cases, predominantly, but not exclusively, in HER2-positive subtype. Using patient-derived, epithelial/neuroendocrine organoid and xenograft models, we map the epigenetic and transcriptional divergence between epithelial and neuroendocrine states arising from a shared mutational background and define a breast cancer neuroendocrine signature. NED involves epigenetic silencing of EpCAM and amplified HER2, while NEUROD1 functions as a master transcriptional regulator of the neuroendocrine fate. NCAM-positive putative circulating tumor cells were detected in patients in whom EpCAM-based detection had failed. Neuroendocrine tumor cells exhibit an FGFR1 dependency associated with NCAM-FGFR1 interaction and mesenchymal FGFR1 splicing. Together, these findings establish NED as a mechanism of escape from HER2-targeted therapy in breast cancer, with implications for disease monitoring and intervention.
