title: Outcomes of Chemoimmunotherapy in Metastatic Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Carcinoma: A Single-Center Clinicopathologic Study.
authors: Moss D, O'Connor CA, Hilmi M et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreatic neuroendocrine carcinomas (PanNECs) are a rare, aggressive subtype of pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms. Based upon similarities to small cell lung cancer (SCLC), advanced PanNECs are commonly treated with platinum and etoposide chemotherapy; however, outcomes remain poor. Although first-line chemoimmunotherapy has improved survival in SCLC, its role in PanNEC is not well defined.
METHODS: We report on a retrospective cohort of 13 patients with metastatic PanNEC treated at Memorial Sloan Kettering with either first-line combined chemoimmunotherapy or first-line chemotherapy alone.
RESULTS: In the first-line metastatic setting, patients who received chemoimmunotherapy (N = 5) demonstrated longer median progression-free survival (17.0 months vs. 2.8 months, P = 0.002) and overall survival (31.0 months vs. 16.0 months, P = 0.031) compared with those who received chemotherapy alone (N = 8). In the second line or later setting, five patients received immunotherapy-containing regimens with a median progression free survival of only 3.0 months (95% confidence interval 1.4 months, Not Reached). Radiologic responses observed in patients receiving chemoimmunotherapy in the first-line metastatic setting were 2 complete responses and 3 partial responses. Germline variants included one patient with a BRCA2 mutation, one patient with co-existing BRCA2 and ATM mutations, and one patient with a MUTYH mutation. Exploratory genomic analyses showed common mutations in TP53, RB1, and KRAS, low tumor mutational burden, and microsatellite stability. Exploratory multiplex immunofluorescence demonstrated heterogenous immune cell infiltrates without a consistent biomarker pattern associated with response.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center cohort, early incorporation of chemoimmunotherapy in PanNEC was associated with improved survival. These findings are hypothesis-generating and support prospective, multicenter evaluation of first-line chemoimmunotherapy strategies in PanNEC (SWOG S2012, NCT05058651) [1].

title: Clinical and radiographic improvement in suspected pulmonary lymphangitic carcinomatosis-associated hypoxemic respiratory failure following iruplinalkib-based treatment in ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma after sequential treatment with ensartinib and lorlatinib: a two-patient case report.
authors: Lin H, Hu Y, Li H et al.
abstract: Pulmonary lymphangitic carcinomatosis (PLC) is an uncommon but life-threatening manifestation of advanced lung cancer and may rapidly lead to hypoxemic respiratory failure. Evidence guiding subsequent anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-directed therapy after prior exposure to multiple ALK tyrosine kinase inhibitors remains limited, particularly in patients with acute respiratory compromise. In this report, we describe two never-smoking women with stage IVB ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma who developed type I respiratory failure. This was accompanied by clinical and radiographic findings suggestive of PLC after sequential treatment with ensartinib and lorlatinib. Case 1 achieved a partial response to first-line treatment with ensartinib for approximately 19 months. At progression, plasma next-generation sequencing identified an EML4-ALK variant 1 fusion with an acquired ALK p.L1196M resistance mutation. During subsequent lorlatinib therapy, the patient developed rapidly progressive dyspnea, diffuse bilateral peribronchovascular and reticular opacities suggestive of PLC according to radiographic findings, and type I respiratory failure. Rapid improvement in oxygenation was observed following initiation of third-line iruplinalkib monotherapy. Case 2 had ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma with an intravascular tumor thrombus on diagnostic biopsy. After ensartinib discontinuation due to grade 3 constipation and subsequent lorlatinib therapy, the patient developed type I respiratory failure, pleural effusion, and progressive bilateral pulmonary abnormalities suggestive of PLC according to radiographic findings. Iruplinalkib was administered in combination with salvage pemetrexed. Following initiation of the respective treatment regimens, both patients showed rapid improvement in oxygenation and radiographic observations of pulmonary abnormalities. Case 1 received iruplinalkib monotherapy, whereas case 2 received iruplinalkib and pemetrexed; therefore, treatment-specific attribution was not possible in case 2. No adverse events attributable to iruplinalkib were observed. In these two patients, initiation of iruplinalkib-based treatment was followed by rapid improvement in clinical and radiographic findings, supporting further evaluation of this treatment strategy in similar critically ill patients.

title: Development and Validation of an UPLC-QqQ MS/MS Method for the Determination of Daraxonrasib, a New pan-KRAS Inhibitor, in Dog Plasma and Whole Blood and Its Application to Pharmacokinetic Studies.
authors: Zhang W, Liu Y, Fan A et al.
abstract: Daraxonrasib, an orally administered pan-RAS inhibitor, is undergoing clinical evaluation for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, colorectal cancer, and non-small cell lung cancer. Defining its pharmacokinetic profile is therefore critical for ongoing progress. Accordingly, a simple and sensitive UPLC-QqQ-MS/MS assay was developed and validated to quantify daraxonrasib in canine plasma and whole blood. Proteins were precipitated with a 20:80 (v/v) acetonitrile-methanol solution containing 0.1% formic acid. Chromatographic separation was performed on a Waters ACQUITY BEH C18 column (50 mm × 2.1 mm, 1.7 μm). The mobile phase consisted of 2 mM ammonium acetate and acetonitrile, each containing 0.1% formic acid, delivered at 0.4 mL/min. Multiple reaction monitoring transitions for daraxonrasib and the internal standard were m/z 811.5 → 680.3 and m/z 724.4 → 396.2, respectively. Calibration standards showed linear response from 1.0 to 1000 ng/mL (r > 0.998). The assay met validation criteria for specificity, recovery, limit of quantification, accuracy, and precision. Finally, this validated method was applied to a dog pharmacokinetic study of daraxonrasib. This report outlines the drug's pharmacokinetic characteristics and supports its continued development.

title: A Phase 1a/1b Of Zanidatamab In Combination With Zongertinib In HER2-Mutated Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)
summary: This is a Phase Ia/Ib, open-label study evaluating the concurrent administration of zanidatamab and zongertinib in patients with advanced, unresectable, or metastatic non-small lung cancer harboring HER2 alterations.

title: Prospective multicenter study of murmur localization and stage-associated murmur grading in dogs with echocardiographically diagnosed cardiac diseases: the LISTEN study.
authors: Wess G, Häggström J, Stadler J et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac auscultation remains fundamental in dogs with suspected cardiac disease, but large prospective datasets describing clinician-recorded murmur localization and intensity across echocardiographic diagnoses are limited. This study aimed to characterize point of maximal intensity (PMI) patterns in dogs with echocardiographically diagnosed cardiac abnormalities and to evaluate the association between murmur grade and disease stage in dogs with myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) and dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM).
METHODS: This prospective international multicenter observational study included 6,996 client-owned dogs examined by 50 cardiology-trained veterinarians. Dogs underwent standardized cardiac auscultation at four predefined thoracic locations and transthoracic echocardiography during the same clinical visit. PMI localization was described across cardiac diagnoses, and murmur grade was evaluated in relation to disease stage in MMVD and DCM.
RESULTS: Dogs with MMVD and DCM predominantly had a left apical PMI, whereas congenital outflow tract diseases and patent ductus arteriosus were predominantly associated with a left basilar PMI. Tricuspid regurgitation and ventricular septal defect were more commonly associated with right apical and right basilar PMIs, respectively. In MMVD, murmur intensity increased with advancing disease stage (p < 0.001), and dogs with a murmur greater than soft had higher odds of being in stage B2 or C/D than B1 (OR 35.9, 95% CI 27.6-46.6). In DCM, 25.8% of dogs had no audible murmur. Although murmur grade distribution differed across DCM stages (p = 0.03), intensity did not show a consistent stage-associated increase.
CONCLUSION: Clinician-recorded four-point auscultation identified characteristic regional PMI patterns across several canine cardiac diseases. Murmur grade was strongly associated with disease stage in MMVD but provided limited stage-related information in DCM. Auscultation may support initial clinical assessment and prioritization of differential diagnoses, but echocardiography remains essential for definitive diagnosis and staging.

title: Pegzilarginase and Pembrolizumab for Extensive Disease Small Cell Lung Cancer
summary: The main purpose of this Phase 1/2 study is to determine the safety and efficacy of pegzilarginase in combination with pembrolizumab in patients with ED-SCLC who have relapsed or progressive disease on or within 6 months of platinum-based chemotherapy.

title: Is pneumonectomy appropriate after chemoimmunotherapy? Outcomes of neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy followed by pneumonectomy in the United States.
authors: Caturegli G, Jernigan E, Canavan M et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The appropriateness of pneumonectomy for non-small cell lung cancer after neoadjuvant therapy is not well characterized, and there is concern for substantially greater mortality on the basis of results of trials such as Intergroup-0139. Here, we present current use and outcomes of pneumonectomy after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy.
METHODS: Using the National Cancer Database, we identified and included adults with clinical stage I-III lung adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma who were diagnosed between 2018 and 2023 and treated with neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy followed by lobectomy or pneumonectomy. Three-year overall survival was assessed by Kaplan-Meier. Propensity matching and Cox proportional hazards models were based on patient and tumor characteristics.
RESULTS: The study included 2703 (94%) lobectomies and 173 (6%) pneumonectomies. Patients who underwent pneumonectomy had a more advanced T stage (64% vs 47% T3+, P < .001) but a lower comorbidity burden (71% vs 58% Charlson-Deyo of 0, P = .01). They had greater rates of 30-day unplanned readmission (9% vs 4%, P = .001) and R1+ resection (7.1% vs 3.9%, P = .046) but comparable 90-day mortality (<4.5% vs 2%, P = .24). Unadjusted 3-year overall survival was not significantly different between the 2 groups: 80% for pneumonectomy and 82% for lobectomy (P = .08). Similar trends were observed after propensity-matching for patient and tumor characteristics: 79% for pneumonectomy and 78% for lobectomy (P = .19). On Cox models, pneumonectomy was associated with a greater hazard ratio of mortality, but this was not statistically significant (odds ratio, 1.56; 95% CI, 0.91-2.68; P = .09).
CONCLUSIONS: Pneumonectomy after induction chemoimmunotherapy demonstrated comparable early survival with lobectomy among selected patients in the United States. Use of pneumonectomy after chemoimmunotherapy in appropriate candidates appears reasonable.

title: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy in geriatric patients with non-small cell lung cancer: A real-world analysis.
authors: Dourlain J, Bushara O, Farooq MS et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy has been shown to significantly improve survival in patients with stage IB-IIIB non-small cell lung cancer. However, it is unknown whether geriatric patients experience similar benefits. Using a large national cohort, we studied outcomes of neoadjuvant immunotherapy in geriatric patients with stage IB-IIIB non-small cell lung cancer.
METHODS: Patients with stage IB-IIIB non-small cell lung cancer treated over 24 months (2022-2023) were identified in the National Cancer Database. Geriatric patients were defined as being older than 75 years. Geriatric patients and younger patients aged 75 years or less were compared in terms of treatment intensity, perioperative outcomes, and survival. Kaplan-Meier curves, log-rank tests, and Cox proportional hazards models were used for statistical analysis of survival. Multivariable logistic regression was used to analyze perioperative outcomes.
RESULTS: 21,070 patients aged more than 75 years with clinical stage IB-IIIB non-small cell lung cancer were included in this analysis. Among them, 4467 (21.2%) received surgery and 447 (10.0%) received neoadjuvant immunotherapy, compared with 35.3% and 17.9% of younger patients, respectively (P < .001). Both surgery (adjusted HR 0.34 [0.27-0.43], P < .001) and neoadjuvant immunotherapy (0.39 [0.25-0.63], P < .001) were associated with improved survival in geriatric patients. Geriatric patients who received neoadjuvant immunotherapy also demonstrated acceptable perioperative outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: In a large national cohort, we show that although geriatric patients have lower treatment intensity than younger patients, both surgery and neoadjuvant immunotherapy render a survival benefit while retaining acceptable perioperative outcomes. Whenever possible, standard of care treatment should be pursued in geriatric patients, and age in isolation should not exclude patients from optimal treatments.

title: Methodological Divergence in Oncology HTA: Implications for International Harmonization and the Handling of Uncertainty.
authors: Chen NC, Bullement A, Zemplenyi AT et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: While health technology assessment (HTA) guides public funding decisions under uncertainty, existing research often examines individual methodological issues or high-level decision variation rather than how methodological choices interact throughout the appraisal process. Using immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in non‑small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) as a case study, this study examines how varying methodological choices shape cost‑effectiveness conclusions and reimbursement outcomes between National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) and Canada's Drug Agency (CDA-AMC).
METHODS: Thirty‑five published technology appraisals from NICE and CDA‑AMC through February 2026 were reviewed using a prespecified, systematic approach. Extracted data included pivotal trial characteristics, comparator selection, cost‑effectiveness conclusions, and key modeling assumptions, including modeling methods, time horizon, utility values, survival extrapolation, treatment duration, effect waning, and cure.
RESULTS: Overall concordance in cost‑effectiveness conclusions was 56.3%, with NICE issuing positive conclusions more frequently than CDA‑AMC (83.3% versus 41.2%). Divergence arose from differences in appraisal processes and methodological inputs, particularly comparator selection, reimbursement populations, and long-term modeling assumptions. Approaches to treatment‑effect waning evolved from abrupt loss‑of‑effect assumptions to gradual decline models, though persistence assumptions varied across appraisals in line with data maturity. NICE more frequently explored alternative modeling approaches, whereas CDA‑AMC applied greater scrutiny to indirect evidence and long‑term projections.
CONCLUSIONS: HTA decisions for ICIs by NICE and CDA‑AMC diverged across multiple uncertainty domains, reflecting interacting methodological choices throughout the appraisal process rather than isolated technical factors alone, highlighting the importance of greater alignment in approaches to uncertainty management for future HTA harmonization efforts.

title: Integration of TRM-Cell Infiltration and PD-L1 Expression Improves Prognostic Stratification After Resection of NSCLC.
authors: Tanimura T, Shiohara M, Ueno A et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, including tissue-resident memory T (TRM) cells, are associated with prognosis in patients after resection of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, their clinical significance in the context of tumor immune suppression, such as through expression of programmed cell death ligand-1 (PD-L1), remains unclear. We hypothesized that integrating TRM-cell infiltration with PD-L1 expression would improve prognostic stratification.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 316 patients with NSCLC who underwent curative resection between 2017 and 2020 without perioperative immunotherapy. TRM cells were quantified by CD103 immunohistochemistry using tissue microarrays and digitally analyzed with QuPath. PD-L1 expression was assessed using the 22C3 assay. Recurrence was evaluated using competing-risks analysis. Recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) were analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method and Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: The median TRM density was 54.8 cells/mm2 and was used to define TRM-high and TRM-low groups. TRM-high tumors were associated with non-adenocarcinoma histology and PD-L1 expression ≥1%. Patients with TRM-high tumors showed a significantly lower cumulative incidence of recurrence (p=0.039), whereas PD-L1 expression ≥1% was associated with worse RFS and OS. When combined, TRM-high/PD-L1 expression <1% demonstrated lowest cumulative incidence of recurrence (p=0.017) and significantly improved RFS and OS (p=0.0035 and p=0.0031, respectively). In multivariable analysis, TRM-high/PD-L1 expression <1% was independently associated with lower recurrence (hazard ratio=0.36) and improved RFS (hazard ratio=0.47).
CONCLUSION: The combined assessment of TRM-cell infiltration and PD-L1 expression provides robust prognostic stratification in resected NSCLC and may serve as a useful biomarker for predicting postoperative outcomes.

title: Lactate-Induced PPP1R1B Upregulation Drives Resistance to Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy in NSCLC via IRF3 Dephosphorylation.
authors: Jiang Z, Yuan J, Li G et al.
abstract: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy has improved clinical outcomes in resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, a substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve durable responses, and the mechanisms underlying therapeutic resistance remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified protein phosphatase 1 regulatory inhibitor subunit 1B (PPP1R1B) as a metabolic driver of immunotherapy resistance in NSCLC through RNA sequencing of tumors with differential responses to neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 therapy. PPP1R1B was significantly upregulated in non-responders and correlated with poor prognosis in NSCLC patients. Mechanistically, PPP1R1B directly interacted with IRF3 through the Arg29 residue and promoted dephosphorylation of IRF3 at Ser396, thereby suppressing IRF3 activation and downstream interferon-β (IFN-β) signaling. PPP1R1B-mediated inhibition of IFN-β signaling reduced CD8+ T-cell infiltration and impaired antitumor immunity, ultimately conferring resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in vivo. Blockade of IFN-β signaling abrogated the antitumor effects induced by PPP1R1B depletion, supporting an immune-dependent mechanism. Notably, tumors resistant to neoadjuvant immunotherapy exhibited impaired oxidative phosphorylation and excessive lactate accumulation. Lactate induced PPP1R1B expression through NF-κB-dependent transcriptional activation, linking metabolic reprogramming to innate immune suppression. Collectively, our findings identify a lactate/NF-κB/PPP1R1B/IRF3 signaling axis that drives immune evasion and resistance to neoadjuvant immunotherapy in NSCLC, and nominate PPP1R1B as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for overcoming anti-PD-1 resistance.

title: Electrochemical detection of the ethyl acetate biomarker using a lead-free double perovskite for the early diagnosis of lung cancer.
authors: Singh P, Bansal NK, Alam S et al.
abstract: Early detection of lung cancer biomarkers through sensitive electrochemical sensing is highly important for non-invasive clinical diagnostics. Lead-free double perovskite Cs2PdBr6 microcrystals were synthesized using a chemical precipitation method and deposited onto fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) electrodes to fabricate a dual-mode electrochemical/photoelectrochemical sensor for ethyl acetate (EA) detection (a potential lung cancer biomarker). The Cs2PdBr6-modified electrode exhibited sensitive EA detection under dark and photoradiation conditions over a linear concentration range of 1.0-1000.0 nM. The sensor achieved a sensitivity of 0.315 mA cm-2 nM-1 under dark conditions and 0.373 mA cm-2 nM-1 under illumination. The corresponding detection limits were 0.045 nM and 0.038 nM, respectively, at a low bias voltage of -0.2 V. The device also demonstrated rapid response and recovery characteristics with a response time of 2 s under photoradiation. Furthermore, the sensing platform showed reliable EA detection in simulated urine samples, indicating its potential applicability in complex physiological environments. Machine learning-assisted analysis was additionally employed for accurate discrimination and quantitative prediction of EA concentrations. The obtained results demonstrate that Cs2PdBr6 is a promising lead-free perovskite platform for stable and high-performance dual-mode EA sensing applications.

title: Evolving Cancer Survival in Taiwan Over 25 Years: Nowcasting with the Survivorship-Period-Cohort Model.
authors: Chiang CJ, Tsai DR, Yang YW et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer has been the leading cause of death in Taiwan since 1982, but long-term survival trends remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated 25-year cancer survival trends, including stage-specific outcomes.
METHODS: We analyzed Taiwan Cancer Registry data for patients aged 15-99 years diagnosed with cancer between 1996 and 2021. We estimated the cancer survival index for all sites combined and age- and sex-adjusted 5-year relative survival ratios for individual cancers. The Ederer II cohort method was used for diagnoses before 2018, and the survivorship-period-cohort model was used to nowcast survival for diagnoses in 2018-2020. TNM stage-specific survival was evaluated for 17 cancers diagnosed during 2010-2017.
RESULTS: The 5-year cancer survival index increased from 46.8% in 1996 to a nowcast estimate of 56.2% in 2020. Survival improved most for small intestine, lung, and nasopharyngeal cancers, with lung adenocarcinoma also shifting toward earlier-stage diagnosis. Survival declined for cervical, renal pelvis, bladder, brain and CNS, and gallbladder cancers. Stage-specific survival remained largely stable for most cancers, whereas lung cancer showed clear gains, including across all stages of adenocarcinoma and in late-stage squamous cell carcinoma.
CONCLUSIONS: Nationwide cancer survival improved substantially, but persistent cancer-specific gaps highlight priorities for early detection, treatment, and cancer control.
IMPACT: These population-based estimates provide timely evidence for monitoring cancer prognosis, evaluating cancer-control progress, and identifying cancers and stages requiring greater clinical and public health attention.

title: Evaluating the impact of electronic reminders for primary care physicians on lung cancer-screening rates.
authors: Kamtam DN, Chang CC, Weng Y et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We evaluated the impact of electronic reminders for primary care physicians (PCPs) on lung cancer screening (LCS) rates.
METHODS: The LCS Health Maintenance Due is an electronic health record-integrated tool that alerts PCPs when patients are due for low-dose computed tomography. Eligible patients were assigned a dynamic screening status on the basis of time since last imaging of the chest. Patients assigned as Not Due, Due Soon, or Due On at rollout were categorized as Baseline Screened, whereas those assigned as Overdue were categorized as Baseline Overdue. We retrospectively evaluated LCS rates at 1 year after rollout and evaluated factors associated with up to date screening status.
RESULTS: Among 8346 eligible patients, 779 (9.3%) were assigned to the Baseline Screened group and 7567 (91%) to the Baseline Overdue group. LCS rates increased from 9.3% at rollout to 16% at 1 year (P < .001). Among patients in the Baseline Screened group, 396 (51%) maintained up to date screening at 1 year, with older age associated with greater odds of remaining up to date (odds ratio [OR], 1.53; P = .003). Among patients in the Baseline Overdue group, 963 (13%) achieved up to date screening at 1 year. Family history of cancer (OR, 2.0; P = .005) was associated with increased odds of screening, whereas greater travel distance (>50 vs <15 miles: OR, 0.38; P < .001), Medicaid/Medi-Cal insurance (OR, 0.58; P < .001), and patients who actively smoke (OR, 0.81; P = .007) were associated with lower odds of becoming up to date.
CONCLUSIONS: EHR-integrated electronic reminders for PCPs were associated with significantly increased LCS uptake at 1 year, supporting scalable system-level interventions to improve LCS rates.

title: Gene-radon interaction effects on lung cancer risk: validation of susceptibility loci using archived DNA from German Uranium miners.
authors: Rosenberger A, Bonzheim I, Fend F et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radon exposure increases lung cancer risk, shown in studies on indoor exposure (low exposure) and uranium miners (high exposure). Genome-wide and candidate gene studies have identified DNA variants that interact with occupational radon to modify lung cancer risk.
METHOD: Highly fragmented DNA samples of 611 individuals were genotyped using next-generation sequencing. DNA variant associations could be assessed in 526 out of 611 WISMUT uranium miners with lung cancer. The relative risk of lung cancer per allele (marginal effect) as well as its dependence on radon exposure (gene-environment (GxE) interaction) could be estimated from the enrichment of one allele compared to the distribution of genotypes expected under the HWE assumption (Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium). Exposure to gamma radiation, long-lived radionuclides, fine dust, silicate dust and arsenic was considered in the same way.
RESULTS: For markers from six (UBE2U, CDKN2A, SIRT1, NAV2, ST8SIA2, TP53) of the 10 genes examined, a significant modification of the genetic relative risk for lung cancer due to mining-specific radon exposure [in WLM] was observed.
CONCLUSION: Radon exposure may be the main cause of some of the observed GxE interactions involving UBE2U, CDKN2A and SIRT1, but it may not be the only one. This conclusion is supported by the function of these genes, as based on relevant literature. For another marker of the gene SOX5, a GxE interaction can presumably be attributed to exposure to arsenic. For the remaining genes, no single environmental factor (radon, dust or arsenic) can unambiguously be identified as sole cause of the GxE interaction.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

title: Temporal trends and socio-demographic disparities in COPD-lung cancer co-occurrence mortality in the United States: a 22 year analysis (1999-2020).
authors: Nadeem A, Rizvi SMA, Basaria AAA et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) and lung cancer remain among the leading causes of mortality worldwide, with a high burden reported in the United States. While both conditions often coexist and share risk factors such as smoking and environmental exposure, temporal mortality trends and disparities across demographics remain underexplored.
OBJECTIVE: To analyze age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) associated with the co-occurrence of COPD and lung cancer (COPD-LC) in the United States from 1999 to 2020, with a specific focus on temporal shifts and disparities across sex, race/ethnicity, and geographic regions.
METHODS: Mortality data were retrieved from the CDC WONDER database. The underlying causes of death were identified using ICD-10 codes (J40-J44 for COPD and C33-C34 for lung cancer). AAMRs were standardized to the 2000 U.S.
POPULATION: Joinpoint regression analysis was used to calculate Annual Percent Changes (APCs) and identify statistically significant shifts in mortality trends. Subgroup analyses were conducted by sex, race/ethnicity, and census regions. Mortality associated with the co-occurrence of COPD and lung cancer was identified using multiple-cause-of-death coding.
RESULTS: A total of 587,762 deaths involving co-occurring chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and lung cancer were identified in the United States between 1999 and 2020. Overall age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) declined from 8.904 per 100,000 population in 1999 to 7.128 in 2020. Joinpoint regression demonstrated a three-segment trend, including a non-significant decline from 1999 to 2006 (APC: - 0.40), a significant decline from 2006 to 2018 (APC: - 1.77%), and a non-significant increase from 2018 to 2020 (APC: 0.71%). Sex-stratified analysis showed persistently higher mortality among males, although mortality declined more substantially in males than in females over time. Non-Hispanic White individuals demonstrated the highest mortality burden, whereas Asian or Pacific Islander and Hispanic populations had the lowest AAMRs. Regionally, mortality rates remained highest in the Midwest and South, while the West exhibited the steepest decline. Non-metropolitan areas demonstrated persistently elevated mortality rates compared with metropolitan regions.
CONCLUSION: While mortality among individuals with co-occurring COPD and lung cancer has declined significantly over two decades, demographic disparities based on sex, race, and geography persist. These findings highlight the need for equity-driven public health interventions and early detection strategies tailored to high-risk populations.

title: Analysis of Whole Exome and Transcriptome Sequencing to Identify Prognostic Biomarkers in Patients With Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)
summary:
This is a non-interventional translational research study aiming to comprehensively characterize the genomic and transcriptomic landscape of patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The study will employ whole-exome sequencing (WES) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) on tumor tissue samples and matched germline DNA to identify genomic alterations, mutational signatures, and transcriptomic profiles associated with prognosis and response to immunotherapy.

A total of approximately 300 patients with histologically confirmed NSCLC will be included, comprising both metastatic and early-stage disease. Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor tissue and, where available, fresh frozen samples will be analyzed. Peripheral blood samples will also be collected for germline DNA assessment. The study aims to identify clinically actionable genomic alterations, measure tumor mutational burden (TMB), characterize immune-related gene expression signatures, and investigate associations between molecular findings and clinical outcomes.

In addition, a pilot sub-study will evaluate circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) dynamics in approximately 20 patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC treated with concurrent chemoradiation followed by durvalumab maintenance therapy. Longitudinal plasma samples will be collected at predefined timepoints to assess minimal residual disease (MRD), ctDNA kinetics, and correlations with clinical outcomes including progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS).

The results of this study are expected to improve understanding of tumor biology and immune landscape in NSCLC and support the identification of prognostic and predictive biomarkers for immunotherapy and other treatment strategies.

title: Differences in patterns of relapse and survival after relapse between lobectomy and sublobar resection for stage IA non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Adachi M, Yoshida Y, Takemura C et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: In the Japan Clinical Oncology Group 0802 trial, lung cancer-specific mortality was comparable between lobectomy and segmentectomy despite a higher rate of locoregional relapse after segmentectomy. We evaluated relapse patterns and postrelapse survival following lobectomy or sublobar resection.
METHODS: This single-institution retrospective study included patients who underwent surgery for primary non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) between 2003 and 2022 and subsequently developed relapse. Overall survival was defined as the period from surgery (OS1) or from the date of relapse diagnosis (OS2) to death from any cause.
RESULTS: Among 362 patients with clinical stage IA NSCLC who developed relapse, isolated locoregional relapse accounted for 110 of 297 relapsed patients (37.0%) after lobectomy and 36 of 65 relapsed patients (55.4%) after sublobar resection. Among 59 patients treated with local consolidative therapy for isolated locoregional relapse, the 4-year OS2 rate was 76.4% (95% CI, 64.9%-89.8%). After inverse probability of treatment weighting, the 7-year OS1 rates were 49.3% (95% CI, 42.2%-57.6%) after lobectomy and 64.9% (95% CI, 52.4%-80.3%) after sublobar resection, and the 4-year OS2 rates were 49.6% (95% CI, 42.4%-57.9%) and 62.7% (95% CI, 49.5%-79.3%), respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory cohort of patients who developed postoperative relapse, relapse patterns differed between surgical groups, with isolated locoregional relapse representing a larger proportion of relapse in the sublobar resection group. Long-term survival was observed in selected patients treated with modern postrelapse therapies, including local consolidative therapy. These findings should be interpreted cautiously as hypothesis-generating.

title: Validation of robotic resection without preoperative diagnosis for peripheral clinical T1N0 lung cancer.
authors: Nguyen DM, Villamiziar N, Cotamo LM et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate safety, accuracy, and cost-efficiency of robotic thoracoscopic diagnostic wedge and immediate anatomic resection without preoperative diagnosis of peripheral nodules suspicious of cT1N0 lung cancers.
METHODS: We queried our robotic thoracic surgery institutional database (January 1, 2017, to December 31, 2025) to identify patients with cT1N0 tumors amenable to intraoperative wedge for cancer diagnosis and immediate curative-intent anatomic resection. Data included demographics, preoperative biopsy, operative details, postoperative outcomes, Mayo Clinic cancer score, and estimated costs associated with cancer diagnosis and resection.
RESULTS: In total, 786 patients were included in this study; 585 patients (including 65 having nondiagnostic preoperative biopsy) underwent diagnostic wedge resection: 100 (17.1%) benign and 485 (82.9%) malignant diagnosis. A total of 467 had anatomic resections (1-stage diagnosis and therapy, group 1); 266 patients had preoperative biopsy, with definite cancer diagnosis in 201 (75.8%) and 197 had anatomic resection (2-stage diagnosis then therapy, group 2), whereas 65 (24.4%) nondiagnostic biopsies required subsequent diagnostic resection, and 118 patients had wedge resection only (group 3). Three groups had similar preoperative characteristics. Larger tumors, more lobectomy, and greater incidence of nodal upstaging and costs were observed in group 2. Discordance between intraoperative and postoperative pathology was noted in 11 (2.3%) of 485 patients, with 9 having a history of carcinoma. No complications were reported in 88.6%, 83.7%, and 94.1% of patients in groups 1, 2, and 3, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: 1-stage robotic resection is a safe, accurate, and cost-efficient strategy in this patient population. Preoperative biopsy is useful in patients with a previous history of carcinoma to minimize diagnostic discordance associated with under/over-treatments.

title: Practice patterns and outcomes of local and systemic therapy for single-site metastatic non-small cell lung cancer in the era of immunotherapy.
authors: Esnaola G, Canavan M, Caturegli G et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Prognosis of lung cancer with single metastatic sites in the era of immunotherapy remains poorly described. We used the National Cancer Database to assess how metastatic site and the use of local therapy with systemic immunotherapy is associated with prognosis in the United States.
METHODS: Patients with clinical stage IVA lung cancer treated with immunotherapy were identified in the National Cancer Database (2018-2023). Patients were stratified by metastatic site and treatment: systemic immunotherapy with or without local therapy (immunotherapy + local therapy or immunotherapy). Prognosis was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox survival analysis landmarked at median time from diagnosis to local therapy.
RESULTS: Among included patients (N = 20,214), metastases included lung (N = 5308; 26.3%), brain (N = 3516; 17.4%), bone (N = 3142; 15.5%), distant lymph node (N = 1219; 6.0%), liver (N = 874; 4.3%), and other metastases (N = 6155; 30.4%). A total of 13,890 patients (68.7%) were treated with immunotherapy, and 6324 patients (31.3%) were treated with immunotherapy + local therapy (70.2% received chemotherapy, 27.2% radiation, and 9.8% surgery). Poor 5-year overall survival was associated with bone (20.9%) and liver (15.9%) metastases compared with brain (33.4%). Five-year survival was greater in patients selected for local therapy (30.3% vs 20.5%, P < .001); thoracic and extrathoracic local therapy was associated with greater overall survival compared with extrathoracic local therapy alone (37.7% vs 28.2%, P < .001). Differences in 5-year survival with local therapy varied by metastatic site (10.4% lung, 7.1% brain, 0.1% liver).
CONCLUSIONS: The addition of local therapy to a systemic regimen containing immunotherapy was common for patients with single metastatic sites. Patients selected for local therapy had a more favorable prognosis, which varied by metastatic site.

title: Peripheral immune-inflammatory markers associated with intracranial progression-free survival after Gamma Knife radiosurgery in patients with non-small cell lung cancer brain metastases: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Han W, Wei H, Zeng T et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracranial outcomes after Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) brain metastases vary substantially. Peripheral immune-inflammatory markers may provide additional prognostic information, but their associations with composite intracranial progression-free survival (iPFS) and with documented intracranial progression remain unclear. We therefore evaluated these two outcomes separately.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 104 patients with NSCLC brain metastases treated with GKRS between July 2019 and June 2021. Composite iPFS was defined from GKRS to intracranial progression or death from any cause. Documented intracranial progression was additionally analyzed with death before progression treated as a competing event. Six covariates, predefined before fitting the primary multivariable models on clinical grounds, were entered directly into a composite-iPFS Cox model, a Fine-Gray model, and a cause-specific Cox model. Continuous predictors were modeled continuously, restricted cubic splines assessed non-linearity, and time-varying coefficients addressed non-proportionality. A reduced static prediction model was evaluated as a secondary exploratory analysis with 1,000-resample bootstrap optimism correction.
RESULTS: Intracranial progression preceded death in 79 patients, whereas 25 died without previously documented progression. Median overall survival was 14.65 months (95% CI, 11.3-16.2), and median composite iPFS was 6.50 months (95% CI, 6.0-8.5). At 12 months, the cumulative incidences of intracranial progression and competing death were 63.5% and 17.3%, respectively. In complete-case analyses (n = 89), each doubling of neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) was associated with higher hazards in the composite Cox model (HR, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.10-1.96), time-varying Fine-Gray model (sHR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.03-2.01), and cause-specific Cox model (HR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.14-2.19). CD4/CD8 ratio was associated with composite and cause-specific hazards but not with the Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard. The reduced static model had an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.703 and calibration slope of 0.838; calibration weakened at later horizons.
CONCLUSION: Higher baseline NLR showed the most consistent association with both general prognosis and documented intracranial progression after GKRS. The endpoint-dependent CD4/CD8 findings and the internally validated prediction model remain exploratory and require external multicenter validation before clinical use.

title: Synergistic Promotion of Ferroptosis in Cardiomyocytes by Tumor Cell Secretory Factors and PD-1 Blockade.
authors: Ma X, Li X, Qu F et al.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting PD-1 frequently cause severe cardiotoxicity, yet the mechanisms involving tumor-host crosstalk remain poorly defined. Emerging evidence implicates ferroptosis, an iron-dependent regulated cell death, in cardiac injury during cancer immunotherapy. Primary neonatal murine ventricular cardiomyocytes (NMVCs) were exposed to lung cancer-derived tumor-conditioned media (TCM; tumor-conditioned media) enriched with exosomes, anti-PD-1 antibody, or both. Ferroptotic markers, mitochondrial bioenergetics, inflammatory signaling, and exosomal microRNA cargo were systematically evaluated using standardized biochemical assays, quantitative PCR, and targeted pharmacological rescue experiments. TCM primed cardiomyocytes for ferroptosis by downregulating the GPX4/SLC7A11/Nrf2 antioxidant axis, depleting glutathione, and elevating labile iron and lipid peroxidation. Anti-PD-1 treatment alone induced minimal oxidative stress but synergized with TCM to amplify ferroptosis > 4.7-fold, triggering profound mitochondrial depolarization and upregulating pro-ferroptotic enzymes ACSL4/LPCAT3. Tumor-derived exosomal miR-214-3p and miR-23a-3p directly suppressed GPX4 and Nrf2, mediating cellular vulnerability. The combined insult hyperactivated NF-κB and STING pathways in a mitochondria-dependent manner, markedly increasing pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion. Co-treatment with ferrostatin-1, deferoxamine, or Nrf2 activators effectively reversed ferroptotic markers and restored mitochondrial function. Tumor-derived exosomal factors and PD-1 blockade synergistically drive ferroptotic cardiomyocyte death by crippling antioxidant defenses and amplifying inflammatory signaling. Targeting ferroptosis or its upstream regulators presents a promising cardioprotective strategy for patients receiving cancer immunotherapy.

title: Machine learning, molecular docking, and experimental validation identify shared molecular signatures between idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension and malignant pleural mesothelioma: a retrospective study.
authors: Zhang N, Wang C, Wang R et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) exhibits cancer-like features, yet its pathogenesis remains unclear. Given molecular similarities between IPAH and malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM), this study aimed to uncover shared transcriptomic patterns.
METHODS: GEO datasets for IPAH and MPM were analyzed. Overlapping DEGs and WGCNA modules were identified. PPI network analysis combined with LASSO, random forest, and SVM-RFE was used to identify candidate biomarker genes. A classification model was constructed and evaluated using leave-one-out cross-validation and bootstrap optimism correction. Immune infiltration was evaluated by ssGSEA. Molecular docking and MD simulations assessed drug binding to candidate target proteins. qRT-PCR validated candidate biomarker gene expression.
RESULTS: Six concordantly upregulated and eleven concordantly downregulated DEGs were shared between IPAH and MPM. Upregulated genes were enriched in cell cycle regulation, while downregulated genes were enriched in neutrophil chemotaxis. WGCNA identified 58 overlapping genes. CXCR2, S100A9, and LCN2 were identified as candidate biomarker genes. A ROTS sensitivity analysis confirmed that all 1710 MPM DEGs were reproducible and directionally concordant at the matching FDR <0.05 threshold despite the imbalanced case-control ratio. The classification model achieved AUCs of 0.909 and 0.875 in training and external validation sets, with a LOOCV AUC of 0.879 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.896. Immune infiltration revealed increased Th17 cells but decreased neutrophils in IPAH. CXCR2 and S100A9 expression correlated with neutrophil infiltration; LCN2 expression correlated with metabolic reprogramming. Navarixin showed the strongest binding affinity to CXCR2 (-10.1 kcal/mol). MD simulations confirmed stable binding of the CXCR2-Navarixin complex. qRT-PCR confirmed significant downregulation of all three genes in IPAH patients.
CONCLUSION: This hypothesis-generating study identifies shared transcriptomic signatures between IPAH and MPM, highlighting CXCR2, S100A9, and LCN2 as candidate biomarkers linked to immune dysregulation and metabolic reprogramming. The computational and correlative nature of these findings, together with the limited size of the external validation cohort, requires confirmation through functional experiments and validation in larger, independent, and multicentre cohorts before clinical translation can be considered.

title: Comparison of the performance of clinical classification systems for myasthenia gravis relapse after thymoma resection.
authors: Yao Z, Li H, Yang Z et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize clinically significant myasthenia gravis (MG) relapse/exacerbation after thymoma resection and compare classification systems for risk stratification.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort included 257 patients with thymoma-associated MG who underwent extended thymectomy at 3 centers from July 2009 through November 2025. The end point was new MG symptoms after postoperative complete stable remission, pharmacologic remission, or minimal manifestation status plus verifiable MG-related treatment escalation or rescue therapy. Death without MG relapse/exacerbation was treated as a competing event. Cumulative incidence functions were estimated with Aalen-Johansen and compared with Gray tests; predictors were assessed with Fine-Gray models.
RESULTS: During median follow-up of 41.6 months, 69 relapse/exacerbation events and 21 competing deaths occurred. Cumulative incidence was 20.4% at 3 years and 29.0% at 5 years; 68% and 90% of events occurred within 3 and 5 years, respectively. Among 52 relapse/exacerbation events in patients who underwent surgery in 2018 or later with retrievable treatment-status data, 28 (53.8%) occurred during ongoing immunosuppression and 24 (46.2%) after withdrawal. The a/b phenotype-based grouping of the Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America classification (1/A/B) showed the strongest separation (3-year cumulative incidences, 2.5%, 12.3%, and 56.4%; 5-year cumulative incidences, 7.6%, 29.6%, and 56.4% for groups 1, A, and B). Groups A and B were independently associated with relapse/exacerbation (subdistribution hazard ratio, 2.65; 95% CI, 1.18-5.91; and 10.55; 95% CI, 4.55-24.47).
CONCLUSIONS: Clinically significant MG relapse/exacerbation after thymoma resection clustered in the early postoperative years. The a/b phenotype-based grouping of the Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America classification (1/A/B) provided the most informative risk stratification.

title: Anti-Ma1/Ma2 paraneoplastic neurological syndrome associated with malignant mesothelioma: a case study.
authors: Mousapasandi A, Evans S, Kwon GT
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anti-Ma1/Ma2 paraneoplastic neurological syndromes (PNS) are rare immune-mediated disorders classically associated with testicular germ cell tumours but increasingly recognised in a broader range of malignancies.
METHODS: We report a 74-year-old left-handed man who presented with progressive gait ataxia. MRI of the brain showed T2 hyperintensity in the right amygdala and hippocampus, as well as in the left caudate head. Serum and cerebrospinal fluid tested positive for anti-Ma1/Ma2 antibodies. Despite extensive screening, no malignancy was identified.
RESULTS: Neurological deficits worsened over 2 months, including worsening gait, ataxia, opsoclonus and left arm weakness. High-dose corticosteroids, intravenous immunoglobulin, mycophenolate and rituximab led to modest clinical improvement. 4 months later, the patient re-presented with insidious respiratory distress due to a right pleural effusion. Pleural biopsy confirmed mesothelioma. Anti-Ma1/Ma2 PNS linked to mesothelioma are rare but have been reported.
CONCLUSIONS: For this rare association, previous few cases described neurological symptoms emerging months to years after a mesothelioma diagnosis, while ours is the first to report symptoms preceding diagnosis. Early immunosuppression can provide temporary clinical benefit. A more sustained benefit requires identification and treatment of the underlying malignancy. This case underscores the importance of ongoing surveillance for malignancy in patients with PNS.

title: Treatment-specific Association of H&E-based Stromal Tumor-infiltrating Lymphocytes With Survival in Pleural Mesothelioma Treated With Ipilimumab/Nivolumab or Chemotherapy.
authors: Yamasaki T, Yamanegi K, Ota H et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Pleural mesothelioma lacks robust biomarkers to guide personalized treatment selection. Although stromal tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (sTILs) on hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained sections represent a cost-effective biomarker in various cancers, their clinical significance in pleural mesothelioma remains unclear. This study evaluated the prognostic impact of sTILs in pleural mesothelioma patients treated with platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy or dual immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) using ipilimumab plus nivolumab (Ipi/Nivo).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 179 patients with unresectable pleural mesothelioma who received either platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy (n=127) or Ipi/Nivo (n=52). sTILs were assessed according to the International TILs Working Group guidelines and categorized as high (>10%) or low (≤10%). Overall survival (OS) and associations between sTIL status and clinicopathological characteristics were evaluated.
RESULTS: High and low sTIL status was observed in 82 (45.8%) and 97 (54.2%) patients, respectively. Within each treatment cohort, baseline clinicopathological characteristics were generally well-balanced according to sTIL status. In the entire cohort, sTIL status was not significantly associated with OS (p=0.559). Subgroup analyses according to treatment modality showed no significant association between sTIL status and OS in the platinum-pemetrexed cohort (p=0.664). In contrast, in the Ipi/Nivo cohort, OS was significantly longer in the low sTIL group than in the high sTIL group (p=0.027).
CONCLUSION: sTILs may have treatment-specific prognostic significance in pleural mesothelioma. Notably, low sTIL status was associated with longer survival among patients treated with dual ICI but not chemotherapy. Standardized H&E-based sTIL assessment may provide a simple and accessible approach for refining treatment selection in pleural mesothelioma.

title: Membrane-mediated cooperativity of antigen receptors and CD2 adhesion receptors in CAR-T cell activation
summary: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells exhibit a major defect in antigen recognition, often requiring 100-1000-fold higher antigen densities for activation than the native T cell receptor (TCR). Recent work has traced this defect to the inefficient use of CD2/CD58 adhesion by CAR-T cells and demonstrated that matching the extracellular dimensions of CD2/CD58 and CAR/antigen complexes can dramatically enhance antigen sensitivity. Remarkably, modest nanometre-scale changes in CD2/CD58 dimensions produce orders-of-magnitude changes in antigen sensitivity, while having little effect on T cell activation at high antigen densities. Here, we present a general model for the length-dependent cooperativity of antigen receptors and CD2 adhesion receptors in CAR-T cell activation, combining statistical-physical theory with coarse-grained simulations. The model predicts that the antigen concentration required for activation increases sharply with the length mismatch between antigen-receptor and adhesion-receptor complexes until a critical mismatch is reached, at which the complexes segregate. Beyond this critical mismatch when complexes segregate, antigen sensitivity becomes largely independent of complex length, consistent with experimental observations. For small to moderate mismatches, the antigen concentration required for activation exhibits a Gaussian dependence on length mismatch with a characteristic width of only a few nanometres, explaining how nanometre-scale changes in CD2 length can alter antigen sensitivity by orders of magnitude. Fitting the model to measurements of CD2-length-dependent CAR-T cell activation further enables estimation of characteristic molecular length scales and concentrations of antigen-receptor and adhesion-receptor complexes. These results provide a quantitative physical framework connecting nanometre-scale organization of the cell-cell interface to CAR-T cell antigen sensitivity and highlight molecular dimensions as a design parameter for T

title: Therapeutic Targeting of the TGFβ Pathway Augments CAR T cell Efficacy in Glioblastoma
summary: Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T therapy represents a promising approach to improve outcomes for patients with high-grade gliomas (HGG). Recently, we reported on a phase I trial assessing the local delivery of CAR T cells for HGG. Despite notable clinical benefits to CAR T treatment, clinical responses were highly variable between patients. Here we report that TGF{beta} levels in the tumor cavity fluid (TCF) decreased following CAR T treatment and that lower TGF{beta} levels positively correlated with improved patient responses to CAR T therapy. Patients were stratified based on baseline TGF{beta} levels in the TCF before CAR T therapy. Single-cell RNA sequencing of patient tumor tissues identified significant upregulation of genes associated with angiogenesis and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and IL6 and SLRP pathways in TGF{beta} high patients, while IL2, chemokine signaling and NK-mediated cytotoxicity pathways were significantly upregulated in TGF{beta} low patients. Preclinically, we demonstrated that systemic treatment with a TGF{beta}R1 inhibitor markedly improved CAR T efficacy in syngeneic murine glioma models, correlating with changes in the tumor microenvironment (TME) that benefited both endogenous and CAR T cell phenotype and trafficking. Further studies demonstrated that inhibition of the TGF{beta} pathway in CAR T cells, through either TGF{beta}R1 inhibitor or CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of TGF{beta}R2 (TGF{beta}R2-KO), significantly enhanced CAR T cell expansion and antitumor activity. Collectively, our clinical and preclinical findings strongly indicate that targeting the TGF{beta} pathway could significantly enhance CAR T therapy for patients with high-grade gliomas.
